However, in the interest of the general public who are faced with increased flooding due to urbanization every effort is being made to control runoff from the highway right-of-way.
This improvement will also comply with all rules, regulations and standards adopted by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency and the Illinois Pollution Control Board. The proposed project will therefore consist of all necessary measures to control erosion, sedimentation and water pollution.
Erosion (silt and sediment) control will comply with all adopted rules, regulations, and standards of the State of Illinois. A special provision for water pollution control (soil erosion) is applicable to every highway construction project which supercedes Article 107.30 of the Standard Specifications for Road and Bridge Construction of 1968.
The proposed improvement of Lincoln Highway is in agreement with the Comprehensive Plans prepared by private consulting firms for each affected community. Since the existing alignment of the highway will generally be followed there should be no disruption of present or future land use policies.
The land-use plan developed for Chicago Heights indicates that the area between Thorn Creek and Chicago Road on the south side of Lincoln Highway could eventually become a complete park area with all the homes removed for park purposes in an area several blocks in depth. At the present time, there is no evidence of action by the City of Chicago Heights to implement this portion of the land-use plan.
A park just south of Lincoln Highway along the western edge of Ashland Avenue will not be affected by the improvement.
The remaining park area to be considered is that along Lincoln Highway, in Matteson, adjacent to and to the rear of the cemetery, a short distance east of Crawford Avenue. The Lincoln Highway entrance to the park will be maintained under the proposed project and no park right-of-way will be required.
